summary: Registers an Enumservice for XMPP so that xmpp URIs can be used with ENUM, the system that maps telephone numbers to Internet addresses. It is a standards-track registration.

plainLanguage.summary: A way to look up a phone number and find the chat address that goes with it.

questions: how to map phone numbers to xmpp addresses
how to map a phone number to an xmpp address
can xmpp iris be used in enum
subtitle: Registers the XMPP Enumservice so a phone number's DNS entry can point to an xmpp address.

tldr.problem: ENUM maps E.164 telephone numbers to URIs through DNS, but there was no registered Enumservice for XMPP, the Extensible Messaging and Presence Protocol.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC registers the Enumservice "XMPP" (type "xmpp") for the "xmpp" URI scheme, and says XMPP IRIs MUST be mapped to URIs and that resulting URIs SHOULD NOT contain an Authority Component.
tldr.outcome: An ENUM lookup of a phone number can return an xmpp URI for an XMPP entity. RFC 6118 updates this RFC.

today: RFC 4979 is a Proposed Standard and is updated by RFC 6118. It has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
E.164 Number Mapping (ENUM) uses the Domain Name System to refer from E.164 telephone numbers to URIs. Services used with ENUM must be registered with IANA, following Section 3 of RFC 3761.

The Extensible Messaging and Presence Protocol (XMPP) streams XML elements between endpoints in close to real time. It is mainly used for instant messaging, presence and streaming media services.

RFC 4622 registers a URI scheme for identifying an XMPP entity, as a URI or an Internationalized Resource Identifier (IRI). This Enumservice allows such xmpp URIs, and the URI forms of xmpp IRIs, to be provisioned in ENUM.
sections.plainLanguage: Phone numbers can be looked up to find other addresses. This RFC adds chat addresses to the list of things you can find.

sections.title: The Enumservice Registration
sections.content:
The registration template gives the Enumservice name XMPP, the type xmpp and no subtype. The only URI scheme is xmpp, and the intended usage is COMMON.

The functional specification is short: the resource identified is an XMPP entity.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC fills in a form that names the new service and says its addresses start with xmpp.

sections.title: XMPP IRI and URI Rules for ENUM
sections.content:
An XMPP IRI or URI may contain an Authority Component (Section 2.3 of RFC 4622). Its presence tells the application to authenticate as the user named in the URI instead of using its preconfigured identity. In ENUM, arbitrary clients may discover and use the URIs, so in most cases they cannot authenticate as requested. URIs that result from an XMPP Enumservice record therefore SHOULD NOT contain an Authority Component.

XMPP supports IRIs as well as plain URIs, but ENUM supports only URIs for Enumservices. XMPP IRIs MUST therefore be mapped to URIs for use in an XMPP Enumservice record, following Section 3.1 of RFC 3987.
sections.plainLanguage: Some chat addresses say 'log in as this person'. Strangers looking up a phone number cannot do that, so the RFC says to leave that part out.

sections.title: Example Record
sections.content: The RFC shows a NAPTR record under e164.arpa. Its service field is E2U+xmpp, and its rewrite rule yields the URI xmpp:some-user@example.com.
sections.plainLanguage: One line in the internet's phone book says: for this phone number, the chat address is some-user at example.com.

sections.title: Security and Privacy
sections.content:
General security considerations come from the protocols underneath: Sections 3.1.3 and 6 of RFC 3761 for ENUM and Section 14 of RFC 3920 for XMPP.

DNS is a public database, so anything in an ENUM record must be considered public, and copies could remain after the record is revoked. Records can reveal associations between numbers and their owners, especially if the URIs contain personal identifiers or easily traced domain names. The record itself need not contain personal information, since it just points to a location.

Records pointing to third-party resources can be provisioned on purpose by the domain owner, so a claimed association between a number and an entity could be bogus without identity verification, which is out of scope.
sections.plainLanguage: The phone book is public, so anyone can read it. Someone could also write a wrong chat address next to your number, so do not trust it blindly.

sections.title: IANA Considerations
sections.content: The memo asks IANA to add a new XMPP Enumservice to the 'Enumservice Registrations' registry, according to the definitions in this document and RFC 3761. The required template is in Section 3.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC asks the keeper of internet lists to add one new entry using the form in Section 3.
